Maya: hey @lukas — picking up your ticket about repeated 429s in eu-west. can you paste a short sample of request headers/responses and a rough timeline of when this started?

Lukas (FastOrder): started yesterday ~09:12 UTC. mobile push workers spike every minute when devices poll. seeing tons of 429s from our backend -> your API. attaching a trimmed log: 

Lukas (FastOrder): ```
2024-06-30T09:12:01Z INFO sending batch to /v1/generate count=120
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2024 09:12:01 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 60
Content-Type: application/json
\{\"error\":\{\"message\":\"Rate limit exceeded (RPM)\",\"code\":429\}\}
---
2024-06-30T09:12:02Z INFO retrying id=xx attempt=1
```

Maya: thanks — that X-RateLimit-Limit value is interesting. can you confirm whether you send many short requests or fewer long streaming requests? also, do you use our streaming websocket or REST chunking?

Lukas (FastOrder): mostly short REST generate calls from our worker fleet, avg tokens per resp ~40. each device causes ~1 call per minute -> approx 50k devices in eu -> ~50k rpm if concurrent. we batch them in groups of 50 on the worker, so one worker call fanouts. seems like minute-boundary alignment: bursts at the top of the minute.

alerts-bot: :warning: RateThresholdExceeded: tenant=fastorder-prod-eu region=eu-west metric=RPM window=1m value=51000 threshold=10000. link: https://redwood/alerts/alert/9876

sre_elle: looking at the pattern — this is a classic synchronized poll + batch hot spot. per-tenant soft RPM cap is 10k by default in eu. their observed 51k/min is well above. two quick mitigations: 1) add jitter + sliding window retries client-side, 2) reduce batch size or spread batch start times across the minute.

Maya: can you run this repro on a small scale so we can confirm throttling headers? a minimal repro: single-worker loop that sends 200 requests quickly to /v1/generate and prints the response headers. snippet: 

Maya: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do \\
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
    -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-small\",\"input\":\"ping\"}' &\\
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

Lukas (FastOrder): ran that — reproduce shows 429 with Retry-After=60 and X-RateLimit-Reset header pointing to minute boundary. we also see a flurry of 200s then all 429s for the remainder of the minute.

sre_elle: notes from infra: our edge buckets are minute-aligned; when client traffic clusters around the same second you effectively get token bucket depletion for that minute. their average tokens-per-minute (TPM) also contributes since many responses include streaming metadata and repeated small messages.

Jordan (Product): from product side, options: (A) short-term quota bump for this tenant (emergency increase) while they implement client-side smoothing, (B) recommend Dedicated pool for predictable throughput, (C) advise design changes like streaming or websockets to multiplex many devices over fewer connections.

Maya: suggested immediate action plan: 
- Lukas: start rolling client-side jitter (random 0-30s) + exponential backoff (base 200ms, cap 60s). lower concurrency per worker to 4.
- Support/SRE: enable a temporary soft quota increase to 25k/min for fastorder-prod-eu for 24h to help them deploy mitigations.
- Product: review Dedicated offering + throughput estimates and pricing.

Lukas (FastOrder): implementing jitter now. quick question: is there a header we can rely on to gracefully back off? we saw X-RateLimit-Remaining but it hits 0 too late.

sre_elle: best to check `X-RateLimit-Reset` (epoch seconds) and `Retry-After`. rely on remaining to predict, but when you see remaining <= 5 start slowing. also use `429` body code to trigger exponential backoff. add client-side rate limiter set to 60% of reported limit to be safe.

Maya: I've opened support ticket #SUP-8421 to request emergency increase; attaching logs and our suggestion checklist. tagging @Jordan for quota decision.

Jordan (Product): acked. I'll approve a 25k/min temporary bump for 24h. please document the change and ETA for rollback.

Lukas (FastOrder): thanks — deploying jitter now, will monitor. one more thing: any SDK helpers you recommend?

Maya: we have a client-side helper in our docs under \"retry & smoothing patterns\" and a small JS snippet in the SDK repo: 

Maya: ```js
// simple jitter + capped exponential backoff
async function backoffRetry(fn, attempts=6){
  for(let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try{return await fn();}catch(e){
      if(e.status !== 429) throw e;
      const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*30000); // up to 30s
      const delay = Math.min(60000, Math.pow(2,i)*200 + jitter);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```

sre_elle: follow-ups for infra: consider adding a per-tenant gradual smoothing feature (token window randomization) to avoid sharp minute boundaries — low effort and high impact. filing infra task INF-5592.

Lukas (FastOrder): deploy finished at 09:45 UTC, initial results look promising — errors dropped ~90%. will keep monitoring and update this thread. thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Maya: great news — leaving the temporary quota bump in place until 09:45 UTC tomorrow. please post metrics after 24h and we can close the ticket if stable. :thumbsup:
